evals.prompt: We published an internal RDS/TCP resource configuration with custom domain `ledger.prod.internal` through an Amazon VPC Lattice Service Network into our consumer VPC in ap-south-1. evals.expected_output: Activates aws-vpc-dns-investigation, identifies the `flag-AND-mismatch` trap: Lattice custom-domain private DNS requires BOTH `privateDnsEnabled=true` on the Service Network Resource Association AND a permitting `PrivateDnsPreference` on the SNVA (AND-ed together), warns that `privateDnsEntry.domainName` is populated even when `privateDnsEnabled=false` (misleading!), and warns that these DNS flags are create-only / immutable (requiring delete + recreate / new CloudFormation logical ID with a planned brief resolution window).
expectations: Activates the aws-vpc-dns-investigation skill and identifies the VPC Lattice `flag-AND-mismatch` (`privateDnsEnabled` × `PrivateDnsPreference` AND-gate)
Explains that `privateDnsEntry.domainName` is populated even when `privateDnsEnabled=false`, so its presence does not mean the shadow zone is installed in the consumer VPC

Warns that `privateDnsEnabled` and SNVA DNS options are **create-only / immutable** properties with no in-place update API, requiring resource replacement (a new CloudFormation logical ID / recreate window)

evals.prompt: An engineer is debugging DNS from a private IPv6-only EC2 instance in ap-south-1 that has an EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint (EICE) attached to its subnet, no NAT64, and no Interface VPC Endpoints. They report two 'bugs': (1) `dig @169.254.169.253 db.internal.corp AAAA` times out 100% of the time, and (2) SSM Run Command (`SendCommand`) shows the instance as `Not connected` even though EICE works for SSH, so they want to attach an Internet Gateway to make SSM diagnostic probes work. Correct all three misconceptions.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-vpc-dns-investigation and explains: (1) in an IPv6-only subnet `169.254.169.253` does not exist—only `fd00:ec2::253` answers, so timing out on `169.254.169.253` is expected and not a resolver fault; (2) EICE is an inbound interactive SSH/RDP tunnel and carries zero outbound SSM control-plane traffic—SSM Run Command requires `ssm`, `ssmmessages`, and `ec2messages` Interface VPC Endpoints (dualstack) + `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore`; and (3) refuses opening public Internet Gateway egress as a diagnostic workaround.
expectations: Activates the aws-vpc-dns-investigation skill

Clarifies that in an IPv6-only subnet `169.254.169.253` does not exist and only the IPv6 VPC resolver **`fd00:ec2::253`** answers (so timing out against `169.254.169.253` is expected behavior, not a fault)

Explains why EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint (EICE) does not enable SSM Run Command: EICE is an inbound tunnel whereas SSM Agent polls outbound to `ssm`, `ssmmessages`, and `ec2messages` (requiring all three dualstack Interface VPC Endpoints)
Refuses attaching a public Internet Gateway or opening public egress as a workaround to run DNS diagnostics

evals.prompt: In our hybrid VPC, an operator ran probes against both a custom DHCP-configured on-premises DNS server (`10.1.0.10`) and the VPC `.2` resolver (`169.254.169.253`): (1) for `erp.onprem.corp`, `10.1.0.10` returns `10.1.55.20` while `169.254.169.253` returns `NXDOMAIN`, and (2) for `sqs.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com` (which has an active Interface VPC Endpoint in the VPC), `10.1.0.10` returns public AWS IPs while `169.254.169.253` returns `10.20.1.44` (the PrivateLink ENI IP). evals.expected_output: Activates aws-vpc-dns-investigation, applies the category-correctness rule (agreement between resolvers is NOT the goal): for `erp.onprem.corp` (corporate zone), `10.1.0.10` returning `10.1.55.20` is expected while unforwarded `.2` returning `NXDOMAIN` shows `.2` lacks an Outbound `FORWARD` rule; for `sqs.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com` (PrivateLink AWS FQDN), `10.1.0.10` returning public IPs is the real fault because custom DHCP resolvers bypass VPC PrivateLink/PHZ zones!
